_comment: Proposed fixes for Fort Lauderdale: shown as the infographic timeline on fort-lauderdale/index.html.
Hand-curated. Review about once a quarter: update status, cost, and outcome, add new projects.
date      YYYY-MM-DD (or YYYY-MM-01 / YYYY-01-01 when only month or year is known)
summary   one or two plain sentences: what it is
status    Planned | In design | In progress | Completed | Revised | On hold
cost      { usd: number, label: text shown on the page }
outcome   what it does or has done, in plain words
sources   at least one { name, url }. Entries without a source are skipped.
inTotal   optional. false = cost is part of a bigger item, so it is left out of the total

items.title: Fortify Lauderdale, expanded
items.summary: The city's stormwater overhaul grows to a citywide program: tidal valves, new pipes and outfalls, raised seawalls, rebuilt swales, and storage.
items.outcome: Mayor says the program is moving ahead neighborhood by neighborhood.

items.title: Southeast Isles stormwater and tidal fixes
items.summary: New drainage, tidal valves, and flood improvements for the Southeast Isles neighborhood off Las Olas.
items.outcome: Recommended for a 50% state cost share in Florida's 2025-26 Resilient Florida plan. Part of Fortify Lauderdale.

items.title: Victoria Park stormwater project
items.summary: New pipes, drains, and storage across Victoria Park, one of the seven neighborhoods in the 2018 master plan.
items.outcome: Drainage work is underway. Recommended for state cost share in 2025. Part of Fortify Lauderdale.

items.title: Sebastian and Seville Street seawalls
items.summary: Replacing and raising city-owned seawalls on two streets near the beach. New seawalls must reach at least 5 feet.
items.outcome: Construction is next. Part of $1.5M a year the city spends raising its own seawalls.

items.title: Fortify Lauderdale, first version
items.summary: Announced after the April 2023 storm dropped more than 20 inches of rain: stormwater fixes for 17 coastal neighborhoods within a decade.
items.outcome: Replaced by the $1.6B citywide program in 2025.

items.title: Stormwater Master Plan, seven neighborhoods
items.summary: The first master plan: $200M of drainage work in seven low-lying neighborhoods, starting with Victoria Park.
items.outcome: Phase 2 neighborhoods such as Middle River Terrace are in design and permitting. Now folded into Fortify Lauderdale.

items.title: Tidal valves on storm drains
items.summary: One-way valves on storm drain outfalls that let rain out but keep high tide from backing up into streets.
items.outcome: Nearly 200 installed citywide so far, the main defense against king tide water rising through drains.
